simple.meaning: קָרַץ (qârats) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to pinch , i.e. (partially) to bite the lips , blink the eyes (as a gesture of malice), or (fully) to squeeze off (a piece of clay in order to mould a vessel from it).” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 5 times across Job, Psalms, Proverbs, beginning at Job 33:6. Its contexts include kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to קָרַץ (H7169).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.

occurrences.englishText: Behold, I am toward God even as you are.
Don’t let those who are my enemies wrongfully rejoice over me;
who winks with his eyes, who signals with his feet,
One winking with the eye causes sorrow,
One who winks his eyes to plot perversities,
